title: Streaming chunk idempotency and rate-window reconciliation for accurate token metering
creator: Amrita Singh
description:
Problem statement:

We continue to observe small but material discrepancies between tokens emitted by the serving runtime (request-level logs) and tokens recorded in the metering pipeline for streaming responses. Root causes appear to be a combination of: 1) reconnect/resume semantics that cause partial chunks to be retransmitted and double-counted, 2) chunk boundary tokenization differences when streaming chunk split/merge happens, and 3) race conditions between the rate-limiter's token window accounting and the async commit path in the metering aggregator.

Impact: customers see overbilling in a subset of streaming-heavy products; internal alerts show "metering-mismatch" rate ~0.18% on high-volume tenants, exceeding SLO of 0.05%. Rate-limit enforcement can be overly permissive or overly strict due to the mismatch between in-flight uncommitted tokens and the rate-window calculation. This causes both incorrect throttles and billing errors.

Goals: 1) Guarantee idempotent token accounting for streaming sessions (reconnects/resumes) with strong invariants, 2) Reconcile rate-window enforcement with uncommitted in-flight tokens so quotas reflect real usage, 3) Provide an automated audit and correction job to remediate historical mismatches and issue customer credits where appropriate.
reproduction_steps:
1) Enable streaming verbose logging for a test tenant.
2) Start a long streaming generation that emits ~200 tokens across multiple chunks.
3) Simulate a network blip and client reconnect that requests resume from last acked chunk.
4) Observe serving logs (stream frames) vs metering events (kafka metering-topic).
Expected: total tokens in metering equals tokens served.
Observed: metering count > serving count due to retransmitted partial chunks being counted twice; in some cases tokenization differs if chunk boundary splits a multi-byte tokenization unit leading to +1 token due to tokenizer rounding.
root_cause_analysis:
We traced the flow and found three correlated issues: 1) The stream producer emits a frame-level id that is not forwarded to the metering pipeline; metering deduping is therefore done at a coarse session-level which can't differentiate retransmits. 2) The metering pipeline accepts chunk token_count provided by the runtime without re-tokenizing when chunk boundaries are merged — small tokenizer variance can accumulate. 3) The rate limiter calculates 'available tokens' only from committed metering DB counts, ignoring uncommitted in-flight tokens buffered in the aggregator, leading to windows drifting under high concurrency.

Trade-offs considered:
- Always re-tokenizing chunks in the metering pipeline: most accurate but expensive CPU on the pipeline and increases SLO risk.
- Relying on the runtime-provided token counts with stronger idempotency keys: cheaper but requires a small runtime change.
- Enforcing rate-limits only at ingress (fast path) vs at commit time: ingress-only is low-latency but can allow temporary overuse; commit-time enforcement is strict but requires backpressure support for streaming sockets.

Decision: implement idempotency and sequence-based deduping in the metering pipeline coupled with a lightweight re-tokenization validation sample (1% of chunks) to detect tokenizer drift. Update the rate-limiter to account for 'in-flight reserved tokens' (per-session checkpoints) so enforcement reflects pending usage. This balances correctness, cost, and rollout risk.
solution_outline:
1) Runtime change (small): attach stream_chunk_id (uuid per chunk) + session_epoch (increment on reconnect) to every streaming frame and include runtime_token_count.
2) Metering pipeline changes:
   - Use (customer_id, session_id, session_epoch, stream_chunk_id) as dedup key.
   - Maintain a per-session committed_offset pointer in metering DB (Redis + durable backup) for quick idempotency checks.
   - When a new chunk arrives: if dedup key seen -> ignore; else validate runtime_token_count against a cached tokenizer for suspect samples.
   - Emit committed token delta events to billing topic only after dedup decision.
3) Rate limiter changes:
   - Track reserved_in_flight_tokens per session and per-customer (in Redis).
   - On chunk accepted for streaming, reserve tokens immediately (atomic increment); on commit or drop, decrement. Enforcement checks available_quota = quota_window - committed_tokens - reserved_in_flight_tokens.
4) Audit/migration:
   - Backfill job that correlates serving frames, metering-topic events, and commit logs to compute mismatches per customer.
   - Generate corrective adjustments and credits for mismatches beyond threshold, with manual review for large adjustments.
5) Telemetry and alerts: mismatch_ratio, dedup_hit_rate, reserved_vs_committed_ratio, token_validation_fail_rate.
acceptance_criteria:
- Streaming sessions with simulated reconnects show 0 duplicate token counts in metering for 1M test tokens.
- Mismatch ratio for production tenants drops below 0.05% within 48 hours of canary rollout.
- Rate-limit behavior remains stable: no customer experiences sudden throttles beyond planned canary; enforcement tests pass.
- Audit job produces a reconciled ledger and a proposed credit batch with <0.1% false positives on a sample of 10 tenants.
- Unit and integration tests added; CI coverage for metering de-dup logic >= 90%.
implementation_notes:
- Add new protobuf schema field to streaming frame: chunk_id (string), session_epoch (int32), runtime_token_count (int32). Backwards compatible: if absent, pipeline falls back to current behavior and marks chunk as 'legacy'.
- Metering pipeline component changes in kafka-consumers/metering-aggregator service. Use Redis for hot checkpoints and Postgres for durable ledger.
- Token validation sample will call tokenizer microservice in a throttled path (100 qps global). Keep sampling at 1% by default, configurable per-customer.
- Use compare-and-set semantics for reserved token increments to avoid races: redis.HINCRBY and versioned key for per-session.
- Add feature flag metering.idempotency.v1 for safe rollouts.
- Add schema version bump and migration plan for older entries.
tests:
- Unit tests: dedup key handling, session_epoch bumps, reservation increments/decrements.
- Integration: end-to-end test harness that runs a fake runtime client, induces reconnects, asserts metering topic emits exactly once per chunk.
- Load: 1k concurrent streaming sessions for 1 hour on staging to validate Redis checkpoint scaling and rate limiter headroom.
- Fuzz: chunk boundary injection to ensure tokenizer sampling picks up drift.
- Canaries: 5% traffic -> 25% -> 100% with health checks at each stage.
rollout_plan:
Phase A (staging): enable feature flag, run full tests, validate metrics.
Phase B (canary): 5% production traffic for 48h with strict monitoring. If dedup_hit_rate < 99.99% or mismatch_ratio decreases and no unexpected throttles, progress to 25% for 72h.
Phase C: 100% rollout and run backfill audit.
Fallback: disable metering.idempotency.v1 flag which returns pipeline to legacy behavior if critical failure detected.
Communication: Notify CS + billing ops before canary and after full rollout with data on adjustments and endpoints for appeal.
migration_and_audit:
- Run a correlation job (kafka->serving logs->metering DB) to compute per-customer delta for the last 90 days.
- Flag customers with >0.5% positive delta or absolute >$500 mismatch for manual review.
- Generate credit proposals in billing system and record adjustments as draft entries.
- Build a small console view (internal) for billing ops to inspect mismatch shards and approve credits.
- Timeline: audit job run during canary and final run post 100% rollout. Expect run time ~8 hours for 90 days of data on current cluster; optimization may be required.
telemetry:
Metrics to add/observe: 
- meterer.dedup_hits (counter)
- metering.dedup_misses (counter)
- metering.mismatch_ratio (gauge by customer)
- billing.reserved_vs_committed_ratio (histogram)
- tokenizer.validation_failure_rate (counter)
- rate_limiter.rejected_by_reserved (counter)
- end2end.metering_latency_p95
Alerts:
- mismatch_ratio > 0.1% for >1h => P1 (notify eng + billing ops)
- dedup_miss_rate increased by >5x baseline => P0 (investigate immediately)
- reserved_vs_committed_ratio > 2.0 => Investigate potential leak in reservation accounting.
notes:
Follow-on work: evaluate moving tokenizer checks to a dedicated validation pipeline to decouple CPU cost from main metering path. Consider a future enhancement to stream-level soft quotas to give clients better UX when they approach quotas.

SLA discussion: billing ops requests a coordinated customer notification plan for any credits applied. Work with legal if any high-value corrections affect contracts.
